GVaverage

Source: vignettes/articles/criterion-gvaverage.Rmd
criterion-gvaverage.Rmd

GVaverage is the mean genetic variance of the training individuals, the trace of their relationship matrix divided by nn (TSDFGS returns the trace).

Type Genomic variation
Direction Larger is better
Uses a test set no (a test set given to optTrain() is ignored)
Score a given set gv_average_score()
Search with it optTrain(method = "GVaverage")

Definition

tr(G)=‖X‖F2/p\mathrm{tr}(G) = \lVert X\rVert_F^2/p. Maximizing it favors individuals far from the population center.

Use in TSDFGS 

library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
gv_average_score(geno[1:50, ])
## [1] 4012.101
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "GVaverage",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
##  [1] 403 348 311 136 339 313 379  65  33 185 399  51 329 301 244  69 179 122 391
## [20] 335 350  97 382  18 298 323 216  12  27 296  20  44 312 305  10  40 189  52
## [39] 376  16  67 128 162  77  36 389 347 245  32  82

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see How the scores are computed. Use min.iter larger than 300 on real data and check fit$converged.

Original work

Chen, S.-P., Sung, W.-H., & Liao, C.-T. (2024). Constructing training sets for genomic selection to identify superior genotypes in candidate populations. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 137, 270. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-024-04766-y

Fernández-González, J., Akdemir, D., & Isidro y Sánchez, J. (2023). A comparison of methods for training population optimization in genomic selection. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 136, 30. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-023-04265-6

Repository or website of the original authors: R package TSODBG of Chen et al. (2024): github.com/spcspin/TSODBG (GPL >= 3).

License review

Formulas and algorithms are ideas and methods, which copyright does not protect. Where an original package is under a GPL license, we read it to check our results and credit it; TSDFGS is GPL-3, which is compatible with GPL-3 and GPL (>= 3) code. This is our reading of the public record, not legal advice; see the license review.
